key_insight: A rubric-based evaluation found that frontier language models performed much better on low-stakes clinical criteria than on the highest-priority safety-critical criteria.
clinical_relevance: In clinician-authored reasoning tasks, the models missed many critical steps, suggesting that open-ended medical AI still needs careful human oversight and task-specific validation.
method: Five difficult clinician-authored scenarios across four specialties
Each task used an atomic, weighted MECE rubric with 25–62 criteria (184 total)
Three frontier models were compared: GPT 5.4, Claude Opus 4.7, and Gemini 3.1 Pro
evidence_signal: Mean rubric pass rates were 0.47 for Claude, 0.39 for GPT, and 0.37 for Gemini, while critical weight-5 criteria passed only 32.4–41.7% of the time.
watch_item: The dataset is very small and preliminary, so results are useful for benchmarking methods but not yet for broad clinical generalization.
paper_title: A rubric-based controlled comparison of frontier language models on expert-authored clinical reasoning tasks
